thread:
devon: FYI BrightCart (ticket BC-842) just hit a bursty wave of 429s and p95 ~700ms on their dedicated pool this morning. They say it recurs every ~7-8m. I can see autoscaler flips 1->5->1 within ~6-9m windows.

sre-bot: alert: dedicated-pool=dedicated-eu1-bc - scale_events: 2025-03-11T08:10:12Z scale 1->5 reason=queue_spike; 2025-03-11T08:16:05Z scale 5->1 reason=cooldown_expire

anya: oncall taking this. can you dump the pool id, last 30m qlen/reqs and a sample of 429 logs? :mag:

devon: pool=dedicated-eu1-bc. quick notes: spikes line up with a tenant job tenant-bc-batch that fires a heavy job every ~7-8m. snippets below.

maria: my hunch is noisy neighbor. can we get per-tenant queue and conn_count? try these prometheus queries: 

```
sum(rate(redwood_requests_total{pool=\"dedicated-eu1-bc\"}[1m])) by (tenant)
max_over_time(queue_length{pool=\"dedicated-eu1-bc\"}[5m]) by (tenant)
```

samuel: customer also reported intermittent 401s during these windows. likely token refresh storms from their SDK retrying on failures which amplifies the peak QPS. not billing-related but worsens the churn.

devon: did a quick repro with our support harness: steps below reproduce the sawtooth almost exactly.

Repro steps (support harness):
1) spawn 60 RPS of small chat completions from tenant-bc-batch for 90s
2) wait 300s
3) repeat 3 times

curl used: 

```
for i in {1..540}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate \\
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $BC_BATCH_TOKEN\" \\
  -d '{\"model\":\"open-quant-3b\",\"input\":\"ping\"}' &\ndone
```

observed behavior: pool spikes to 5 (warmup), then cooldown drops to 1 and we hit cache cold start + capacity deficit -> p95 spikes and 429s while instances spin up and KV caches refill. token refresh retries add a second wave.

ops-liz: immediate mitigations:
- set min_replicas=3 on dedicated-eu1-bc
- bump cooldown to 180s and cap max scale step to 2
- enable prefix prewarm for that pool to reduce KV cold latency
- enforce tenant-level burst limits for tenant-bc-batch (sustained 40rps, burst 80rps)

CLI to apply: 

```
redwoodctl dedicated update --pool dedicated-eu1-bc --min-replicas 3 --cooldown 180s --max-scale-step 2
redwoodctl tenant update-rate-limit --tenant tenant-bc-batch --pool dedicated-eu1-bc --sustained 40 --burst 80
```

anya: applying now, will stand by and monitor. also add an alert: scale_flap >= 3 events in 15m.

devon: applied at 08:42Z. initial 30m look shows fewer drops to 1. posting before/after: https://graphs.internal/redwood/pools/dedicated-eu1-bc?range=1h

maria: after change: qlen still spikes from the batch job but replicas stay at 3 instead of falling to 1. prewarm cuts p95 by ~200-300ms. also reduced token refresh storms by clamping client retries.

devon: customer confirms latency improved and 429s largely gone. they'll smooth their batch schedule too. ops will send a best-practices note about smoothing bursts and using backoff.

sre-bot: check: scale_flap_detector: events in 60m before change = 7, after change = 1. marking incident mitigated. :white_check_mark:

anya: follow-ups:
- propose default pool min_replicas=2 for RapidScale customers with a flag to opt into aggressive scaling.
- engineering: investigate hysteresis based on rolling median queue_length (5m) instead of instant max to avoid reacting to single-sample spikes. consider tenant-aware prewarm that proactively loads KV for top-tenants when scaling.

maria: noted. I'll spin up a design doc draft for hysteresis + tenant prewarm and link it here tomorrow.

devon: closing thread for now. will reopen if BC reports regressions. thanks everyone :heart:
